answer: A reputation bond that grows with verified work makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a deposit that only unlocks after sustained, useful service, so spinning up thousands of clones costs real capital. Like a plume rising through an ocean current, a genuine track record is hard to fake at scale, while a tundra of idle sock-puppets earns nothing and forfeits its bond. Attackers pay per identity; honest agents earn it back.
